newsitem.title: MONACO: Monaco launches low-key 700th birthday party.
newsitem.headline: Monaco launches low-key 700th birthday party.

text.p: Tiny Monaco begins a 10-month party on Wednesday to mark its 700th birthday but it will be mainly a family affair.
The highest-ranking foreign celebrity expected at the opening ceremonies on the Riviera rock principality is the Vatican spokesman.

Several thousand local residents, tourists and other well-wishers were to gather for a morning mass, followed by the dedication of a statue and a speech by Prince Rainier III, the 29th member of the Grimaldi dynasty to rule the lilliputian state since 1297.

More than $200 million has been set aside for celebrations, which are to last through October and include sporting events, car races, concerts, art shows, plays -- and a meeting of the International Whaling Commission to mark the principality's marine and environmental dedication.

The festivities mark the 700th anniversary of the day that Francois Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, sneaked into the Genoese-controlled fortress, let in his own soldiers, and established a dynasty which claims to be the longest-serving in Europe.
But this sliver of Riviera real estate in the southeastern corner of France, is best known today for what is officially referred to as "the princely family" headed by Rainier.
The much-photographed but star-crossed family, has been in the public eye ever since Prince Rainier married American film star Grace Kelly in 1956.
Kelly died in a 1982 car crash but the rest of her family has remained ever since on the glossy covers of photo magazines.
In addition to the white-haired Rainier, 73, who has reigned since May 1949, there is Prince Albert, slightly balding at 38, and the striking Princesses Caroline, 39, and Stephanie, 31.

Albert, who his father says still needs more experience to be able to take over, complained recently that all the media attention given him and his sisters was detracting from Monaco's economic and cultural successes.
"This is not a festival but a commemoration," said Isabelle Peters, spokeswoman for the event. "The Prince wanted the celebration to be between the princely family and the people of Monaco."
The principality's mild and sunny climate, low crime rate and lack of income taxes for all but French citizens has spurred economic growth and made Monaco a very desirable place to live.
Among its residents are super-model Claudia Schiffer, ex-Beatle Ringo Starr and a bevy of professional race-car drivers and tennis players.

Though Monaco has less than two square km (one square mile) of territory and can be crossed on foot in half an hour, even many of Monaco's 30,000 residents were likely to stay at home for the day, watching the party live on local cable television, Peters said.
Some 450 journalists were nonetheless expected to cover the day's events.
